analysis: Reviewed all three randomized paired rounds (180 enabled and 180 disabled raw HTTP batches per runtime, 32 events each) for the corrected artifact. Aggregate medians are +1.369% on minimum and +0.354% on latest, with per-round results between -0.948% and +4.333%. The previous artifact's minimum result of +5.114% is retained above rather than discarded. These end-to-end Docker measurements include HTTP, scheduling, queues, file output and JVM effects; repeated runs show variation. Recovery changes offline processing, publication and startup validation, not the measured raw-request/handoff hot path. Current measurements do not reproduce the earlier greater-than-5% aggregate result, but neither establish causality nor a universal sub-5% guarantee. The investigation is bound to this exact report and artifact.
remaining_risk: A controlled representative performance environment is needed to bound collector-only and assembly-path costs. No universal throughput or performance-equivalence claim is made.
